title: AI context cards for ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity & Grok — CardGo.AI
excerpt: Save your context once as encrypted cards, then attach the right one in ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity or Grok with the CardGo Chrome extension. Free to start.
content_html:
Why context cards

Stop re-explaining yourself to every AI.

If you use more than one AI chat, every conversation starts from zero: who you are, what you’re working on, how you like answers. CardGo is context management for AI — small, reusable, encrypted cards you attach only when you choose.

Built-in memory stays in one place

What ChatGPT or Claude remembers about you lives inside that one product. A card goes with you to all five chats.

One profile fits nothing well

A single set of custom instructions has to cover work, health and family at once. A card per part of your life lets you pick what each chat knows.

Your context, not a provider’s copy

Cards are sealed on your device and CardGo’s servers hold only ciphertext. You decide what to attach, and you see exactly what is shared before you send.

How CardGo compares with built-in AI memory

How to use CardGo

Three steps to better AI conversations.

Install the Chrome extension, create a card, and attach it when you chat with AI.

  1. Install the extension

    Add CardGo to Chrome. Your cards will be ready beside the AI chats you use.

    Add to Chrome

  2. Create a card

    Save the context you want to reuse, from your role and goals to your preferences.

  3. Choose a card in your AI chat

    Choose the card you need in ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity or Grok.

    ChatGPTClaudeGeminiPerplexityGrok

Profile, Now, Goals, Guidance, Memory, Timeline, Skills. Fill in what’s useful, skip the rest—empty sections save nothing. Pick one below to see what goes in it.

Privacy by DesignEnd-to-end encrypted

Encrypted before it ever leaves your browser.

Your cards are sealed on your device with a key we never receive. What reaches CardGo is ciphertext — we can sync it, count it, and delete it, but we cannot read it.

What you write

Work

Product design lead · Timezone: Tokyo (GMT+9)

What our servers store

An opaque block of ciphertext.Ciphertext · 412 bytes · rev 7 — and nothing else

  • Your key is born on your device

    The vault key is generated in your browser and never sent to CardGo. No copy, no escrow, no reset.

  • AES-256-GCM, a key per card

    Every card gets its own content key, sealed with the browser’s built-in Web Crypto before it is uploaded.

  • Our servers hold ciphertext

    We sync opaque blobs, sizes, and timestamps. Nobody at CardGo can read a card — there is no key to read it with.

  • A recovery phrase only you hold

    Setup shows a 15-word phrase once and asks you to confirm it. We never store it, so only you can restore a vault.

Encryption protects your cards from us — it cannot protect what you deliberately send to an AI provider. Once you attach a card, that context is governed by that provider’s terms. Read the full privacy policy.

FAQ

Questions people ask before installing

What is an AI context card?

A short, structured block of context you want an AI to have: a Profile, what’s happening Now, Goals, Guidance, Memory, a Timeline and Skills. You write it once in CardGo and attach it to a conversation when it’s relevant — nothing is sent until you do.

Which AI chats does CardGo work with?

ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity and Grok, through the Chrome extension in desktop Chromium browsers such as Chrome, Edge, Brave and Arc. Mobile browsers cannot run extensions.

Does CardGo read my AI conversations?

No. It never reads your chat history or the AI’s replies. The only text the extension looks at is the message box and your own unsent draft, so it can suggest a card — and nothing is attached until you choose it.

What is shared when I attach a card?

Exactly the text you previewed: the card’s sections, added to your message when you press send, inside a visible “CardGo context” marker. Skills are sent only when you invoke one. No other card, no profile. Once sent, that context belongs to your conversation with that provider, under its terms.

Can CardGo read my encrypted cards?

No. Cards are encrypted in your browser with AES-256-GCM, one content key per card, under a vault key generated on your device and never sent to CardGo. Our servers store ciphertext and operational metadata. A 15-word recovery phrase you keep is the only way back into a vault — there is no reset.

Is CardGo a prompt manager or an AI memory tool?

Neither, exactly. Prompt managers store prompts; built-in memory lives inside one provider’s product. CardGo stores context about you and your work — encrypted, portable across five AI chats, and attached one conversation at a time, by you.

Is CardGo free?

Yes. CardGo is free to start, with no credit card. The Free plan includes up to 7 end-to-end encrypted cards that sync across your devices.

content_html_zh:
Why context cards

Stop re-explaining yourself to every AI.

If you use more than one AI chat, every conversation starts from zero: who you are, what you’re working on, how you like answers. CardGo is context management for AI — small, reusable, encrypted cards you attach only when you choose.

Built-in memory stays in one place

What ChatGPT or Claude remembers about you lives inside that one product. A card goes with you to all five chats.

One profile fits nothing well

A single set of custom instructions has to cover work, health and family at once. A card per part of your life lets you pick what each chat knows.

Your context, not a provider’s copy

Cards are sealed on your device and CardGo’s servers hold only ciphertext. You decide what to attach, and you see exactly what is shared before you send.

How CardGo compares with built-in AI memory

How to use CardGo

Three steps to better AI conversations.

Install the Chrome extension, create a card, and attach it when you chat with AI.

  1. Install the extensionAdd CardGo to Chrome. Your cards will be ready beside the AI chats you use.Add to Chrome
  2. Create a cardSave the context you want to reuse, from your role and goals to your preferences.
  3. Choose a card in your AI chatChoose the card you need in ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity or Grok.ChatGPTClaudeGeminiPerplexityGrok

What our servers store

An opaque block of ciphertext.Ciphertext · 412 bytes · rev 7 — and nothing else

  • Your key is born on your deviceThe vault key is generated in your browser and never sent to CardGo. No copy, no escrow, no reset.
  • AES-256-GCM, a key per cardEvery card gets its own content key, sealed with the browser’s built-in Web Crypto before it is uploaded.
  • Our servers hold ciphertextWe sync opaque blobs, sizes, and timestamps. Nobody at CardGo can read a card — there is no key to read it with.
  • A recovery phrase only you holdSetup shows a 15-word phrase once and asks you to confirm it. We never store it, so only you can restore a vault.

Encryption protects your cards from us — it cannot protect what you deliberately send to an AI provider. Once you attach a card, that context is governed by that provider’s terms. Read the full privacy policy.

FAQ

Questions people ask before installing

What is an AI context card?

A short, structured block of context you want an AI to have: a Profile, what’s happening Now, Goals, Guidance, Memory, a Timeline and Skills. You write it once in CardGo and attach it to a conversation when it’s relevant — nothing is sent until you do.

Which AI chats does CardGo work with?

ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity and Grok, through the Chrome extension in desktop Chromium browsers such as Chrome, Edge, Brave and Arc. Mobile browsers cannot run extensions.

Does CardGo read my AI conversations?

No. It never reads your chat history or the AI’s replies. The only text the extension looks at is the message box and your own unsent draft, so it can suggest a card — and nothing is attached until you choose it.

What is shared when I attach a card?

Exactly the text you previewed: the card’s sections, added to your message when you press send, inside a visible “CardGo context” marker. Skills are sent only when you invoke one. No other card, no profile. Once sent, that context belongs to your conversation with that provider, under its terms.

Can CardGo read my encrypted cards?

No. Cards are encrypted in your browser with AES-256-GCM, one content key per card, under a vault key generated on your device and never sent to CardGo. Our servers store ciphertext and operational metadata. A 15-word recovery phrase you keep is the only way back into a vault — there is no reset.

Is CardGo a prompt manager or an AI memory tool?

Neither, exactly. Prompt managers store prompts; built-in memory lives inside one provider’s product. CardGo stores context about you and your work — encrypted, portable across five AI chats, and attached one conversation at a time, by you.

Is CardGo free?

是的。 CardGo is free to start, with no credit card. The Free plan includes up to 7 end-to-end encrypted cards that sync across your devices.
